📌 Fake Migration Sites: When "Upgrade Now" Is the Scam

Main Points
⏺ Protocols regularly retire old contracts, bridges and token versions
⏺ Scammers copy these announcements and push look-alike "migration" or "claim" pages
⏺ This post explains how the trap works and how to check a link

1️⃣ Core Idea — When a project announces an upgrade, deprecation or claim deadline, fake sites appear that look identical to the real app and ask you to "migrate" or "claim before it's too late".
2️⃣ Why It Happens — A real deadline creates urgency. People search for the page, click an ad or a link in a reply, and connect their wallet without checking the address bar.
3️⃣ Example — A project says old contracts will be paused next month. A reply under the post links to a "migration portal". It asks you to sign an approval — and that signature lets the attacker move your tokens.
4️⃣ Red Flags — Links from replies, DMs or search ads, a domain that differs by one letter, requests for your seed phrase, and "unlimited" token approvals for a simple migration.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — Open migration and claim pages only from the project's official site or documentation, bookmark them, read what you are signing, and revoke approvals you no longer need.

Final Thoughts

Real migrations are announced in official channels and almost never require your seed phrase. When a deadline feels urgent, slow down first.

Trump called the nuclear arsenals of the U.S., China, and Russia “unacceptable” after the Shenzhen summit. He also told reporters that “it’s very hard for me to say let’s cut them in half” and that he is “not sure that can ever happen.”

🌐 Cryptocurrency exchange MEXC has announced that it will discontinue its Global Card payment services on Nov. 18 at 15:30 UTC, less than two weeks after U.S. authorities issued an order restricting its access to the American financial system. The exchange did not identify the issuing partner or specify whether its decision was directly related to the recent enforcement action by the U.S. Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN).

📊 During the maintenance period, customers could transfer their remaining card balances to their exchange accounts, while transactions initiated before the suspension remained subject to normal settlement procedures. MEXC had initially described the interruption as temporary but has now confirmed that the service will not resume as scheduled.

🔗 Cardholders could receive cashback ranging from 4% to 10%, with monthly rewards capped at up to 800 USDT depending on their eligibility. Applications were already unavailable to U.S. residents under the exchange’s regional restrictions. Customers using the card for recurring payments have been advised to cancel their subscriptions or register alternative payment methods to avoid interruptions once the card becomes inactive.

Cigarettes cost 23 cents in vending machines that took only quarters, so vendors tucked two pennies inside the cellophane as change. Some smokers found the doubled cents right there.
